Looking at this question about colorectal cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and their response to oxaliplatin:

Key considerations:
- Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are known to be notably resistant to many chemotherapy agents, including platinum-based drugs like oxaliplatin
- Research has shown that while oxaliplatin effectively kills colorectal cancer cells, CAFs in the tumor microenvironment are remarkably resistant
- Studies demonstrate that CAFs can survive chemotherapy exposure at very high rates, which is actually a mechanism by which chemotherapy may inadvertently promote tumor progression (by depleting cancer cells while preserving the supportive stromal compartment)
- At 2 weeks of culture with oxaliplatin, CAFs typically show survival rates in the range of 80-99%

This high survival rate of CAFs in the presence of oxaliplatin is a well-documented finding in colorectal cancer research and is one reason why targeting the tumor stroma has become an area of interest in cancer therapy.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
